questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: When choosing my study destination, it was important to me that it was in an English speaking country as one of my primary purposes with studying a semester abroad was to improve my English skills. It was also important to me that the destination was in a country far from Denmark with a culture different from Danish culture, as I wanted to experience student life in a completely different setting in a country with a different approach to studying law at university level. Lastly, it was particularly important to me that the destination was in a common law country as I wanted to study and become familiar with common law (as opposed to civil law in Denmark).

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy. The University of Melbourne is very exchange student-friendly and provides all the information you need upon arrival.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not receive much assistance. All the information you need is made available online and the few questions I had were answered by the friendly staff at the "Stop 1" service desk. There was also a mandatory orientation event for exchange students when I arrived.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is quite expensive, but, again, so is living on campus. Other than that, there is really not much to know - it was really easy to book.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: As mentioned, the housing available to students (both on and off campus) is really expensive compared to Danish levels - especially considering the limited space you get!

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process was basically just to fil out certain information on a website and submit a few documents. The whole process, step-by-step, was laid out in an e-mail from the university. It was very simple.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: As mentioned above, the whole process, step-by-step, was laid out in an e-mail from the university and further information about each step was available online. If you have any problems or difficulties with the registration process, there is also a phone number you can call to get help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was very succesful and got all the classes I registered for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything will go smoothly if you just follow the instructions you receive from the university.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The academic programme was good, although I was a bit disappointed with the limited array of courses available to exchange students.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses varied a lot, and the graduate level courses were quite difficult as they built on knowledge from prerequisite courses that you have not had as an exchange student. As an example, I had the course "Contracts", which was very difficult as it presupposed knowledge about legal concepts and principles in common law and equity that we are not familiar with in Denmark.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching was very similar to that of UCPH and included both lectures and seminars.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1) Contracts
2) Global Human Rights Law
3) Free Speech and Media Law
4) AI, Ethics and the Law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend the courses listed as nos. 2) - 4) above. These are all great courses that are taught at a level accessible to exchange students and give valuable insights into Australian law within the respective areas of law.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not participate in any non-academic activities, such as clubs, sports, tours etc. However, this was by my own choice and I am sure there were a lot of non-academic activities available for those who wish to participate in such activities.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: As I did not participate in such activities, I am not sure what kinds of activities were available.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: As I did not participate in non-academic activities, I, unfortunately, do not have any recommendations.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There are many great things to see and do in Melbourne and Australia. I definitely would recommend other visiting students to travel as much as possible to the different parts of Australia and experience the incredible nature Australia has to offer.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was extremely easy. Australians are such nice people and the culture is in many respects very similar to Danish culture. In Melbourne, the culture is very relaxed.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I mostly socialized with students from other countries, i.e. visiting students, and therefore do not have much experience with socializing with local students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The thing I found most challenging was the language as Australians use a lot of slang - which can make it difficult to understand what they are saying!

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really loved the very easy-going and relaxed vibe and their love for great coffee and good food.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: First of all, only take courses that have prerequisites if you are up for a challenge - they are inherently difficult to exchange students. Secondly, do not stress about exams. They might seem difficult, but in my experience the exams turned out to be manageable and the examiners were reasonable. Lastly, enjoy your time at the university and make sure you take advantage of the opportunities you have to go explore this amazing country.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I believe I have covered this in the sections above.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part, on a personal level, was definitely that I got meet so many interesting and nice people from many different countries and cultures and that I got to experience the incredible nature in Australia.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge was studying at the university, but I believe this is how it is supposed to be. Although the teaching style is similar to that of UCPH, it is just a challenge to study at university level in another country, where things are just a bit different, everything is in English etc.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: N/A

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
